title: Selenium WebDriver: architecture, drivers and the grid

videos.script: Selenium is the oldest of the three tools in this course, and the one the others are measured against. {{logo}} Its idea fits in one picture. Your test does not touch the browser. It sends requests over HTTP to a small program called a driver, and the driver works the browser. {{three}} That conversation is a W3C standard, so you can hold it yourself, with curl, one request at a time. You will. {{curl}} Each browser has its own driver, and the driver has to match the browser's version. Selenium Manager finds one for you. {{drivers}} Then you add Selenium to the shop's project and write the same kind of test you wrote with Playwright. Open the page, wait for the fruit, add a banana, read the basket. {{test}} Notice what you have to say out loud here that Playwright said for you. That difference is most of lesson 10. {{compare}} Last, the grid. One address in front of many browsers on many machines. You start one on your own computer and point the same test at it. {{grid}}
